data.name: Autophagy
data.description: Cellular recycling process suppressed by mTORC1 and activated upon its inhibition; linked to longevity.
data.description_beginner: The cell's built-in recycling system. mTORC1 normally keeps it switched off; when mTORC1 is blocked, it switches on, clearing out damaged proteins and organelles - and it's linked to longer lifespan.

studies.title: Ulk1-mediated phosphorylation of AMPK constitutes a negative regulatory feedback loop

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: ULK1 phosphorylates and inhibits AMPK in return, showing autophagy signaling is a bidirectional feedback loop, not a one-way switch.

studies.title: Mechanisms of life span extension by rapamycin in the fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster
studies.authors: Bjedov I; Partridge L et al.

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Feeding rapamycin extended fly lifespan through autophagy and reduced translation, and worked even in flies already on a lifespan-maximizing diet.

studies.title: Autophagy genes are essential for dauer development and life-span extension in C. elegans
studies.authors: Melendez A; Levine B et al.

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Worms lacking the autophagy gene bec-1 lost the lifespan-extending benefit of reduced insulin-like signaling - autophagy is mechanistically required for daf-2 (insulin-signalling) lifespan extension and for dauer formation in C. elegans.

studies.title: Inhibition of mTOR induces autophagy and reduces toxicity of polyglutamine expansions in fly and mouse models of Huntington disease
studies.authors: Ravikumar B; Rubinsztein DC et al.

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Drosophila and mouse models of Huntington's disease
studies.finding: Induced autophagy cleared toxic clumped proteins and improved symptoms in fly (rapamycin) and mouse (the rapalog CCI-779) models of Huntington's disease.

studies.title: Overexpression of Atg5 in mice activates autophagy and extends lifespan
studies.authors: Pyo JO; Jung YK et al.

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Mice engineered with extra copies of the autophagy gene Atg5 lived 17% longer and were leaner and more insulin-sensitive.

studies.title: TFEB links autophagy to lysosomal biogenesis
studies.authors: Settembre C; Di Malta C; Polito VA; Garcia Arencibia M; Vetrini F; Erdin S; et al.; Ballabio A

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Showed that TFEB drives a coordinated autophagy and lysosomal gene programme during starvation. In this paper TFEB was regulated by ERK2 phosphorylation; its control by mTORC1 at the lysosome was established in later work (SET2012).

studies.title: MTORC1 functions as a transcriptional regulator of autophagy by preventing nuclear transport of TFEB
studies.authors: Martina JA; Chen Yong; Gucek M; Puertollano R

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Showed mTORC1-dependent TFEB Ser211 phosphorylation: mTORC1 (docked at the lysosome via Ragulator) phosphorylates TFEB on Ser211, which traps it in the cytosol via 14-3-3 proteins. Inhibit mTORC1 and TFEB rushes to the nucleus to switch on autophagy - explaining how mTORC1 controls recycling at the level of gene transcription.

studies.title: Nutrient-dependent mTORC1 association with the ULK1-Atg13-FIP200 complex required for autophagy
studies.authors: Hosokawa N; Hara T; Kaizuka T; Kishi C; Takamura A; Miura Y; et al.; Mizushima N

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Showed the DIRECT brake mTORC1 uses on autophagy: when nutrients are plentiful, mTORC1 physically joins the ULK1-Atg13-FIP200 complex (the autophagy-starter kinase) and phosphorylates ULK1 to keep it off. Starvation or rapamycin releases this brake and autophagy begins.

studies.title: AMPK and mTOR regulate autophagy through direct phosphorylation of Ulk1
studies.authors: Kim J; Kundu M; Viollet B; Guan KL

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Revealed the tug-of-war over ULK1: the energy sensor AMPK phosphorylates ULK1 at activating sites to turn autophagy ON when energy is low, while mTORC1 phosphorylates a different site (Ser757) to keep it OFF and even blocks AMPK from reaching ULK1. Two opposing kinases wired to the same switch.

studies.title: Inhibition of mTOR by rapamycin abolishes cognitive deficits and reduces amyloid-beta levels in a mouse model of Alzheimer's disease
studies.authors: Spilman P; Podlutskaya N; Hart MJ; Debnath J; Gorostiza O; Bredesen D; Richardson A; Strong R; Galvan V

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Connected the longevity drug to a specific age-related disease. Long-term rapamycin prevented memory deficits and lowered toxic amyloid-beta in an Alzheimer's mouse model - and the benefit tracked with INCREASED autophagy in neurons. Suggested that the same autophagy boost that may slow aging could also help clear disease-causing proteins.

studies.title: Molecular interplay between mTOR, amyloid-beta, and Tau: effects on cognitive impairments
studies.authors: Caccamo A; Majumder S; Richardson A; Strong R; Oddo S

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Revealed a vicious cycle: amyloid-beta RAISES mTOR activity, and high mTOR in turn blocks the autophagy needed to clear amyloid and tau - so the disease feeds itself. Rapamycin broke the loop in 3xTg-AD mice, rescuing memory and lowering BOTH amyloid and tau, with autophagy induction shown to be necessary for the reduction in amyloid levels.

studies.title: mTORC1 activity oscillates throughout the cell cycle, promoting mitotic entry and differentially influencing autophagy induction
studies.authors: Joshi JN; Valvezan AJ et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Human and mouse cell lines (synchronised populations; fixed-cell single-cell imaging)
studies.finding: mTORC1 activity oscillates across the cell cycle (lowest in mitosis/G1, highest in S/G2) via the TSC complex, independent of Akt/Mek-Erk; low mTORC1 in G1 sensitizes cells to autophagy induction from the same partial inhibition or nutrient drop -- direct evidence that the TIMING/pattern of mTORC1 activity, not just its average level, shapes autophagy outcome.

studies.title: Urolithin A activates mitophagy via the AMPK-mTOR axis and modulates the gut-ceramide axis to ameliorate cardiac remodeling in HFpEF
studies.authors: Hangyul Song, Chahyeon Yun, Yunju Choi, Wooju Jeong, Yumin Kim, Jaeyoung Kim, Ju-Yeon Lee, Dongryeol Ryu, Sang-Wook Park, Chang-Myung Oh

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Urolithin A ameliorates HFpEF cardiac remodeling in mice by activating AMPK and inhibiting mTOR to restore mitophagic flux, while simultaneously remodeling the gut microbiome-ceramide axis to reduce lipotoxic stress.

studies.title: Molecular and metabolic dysregulation of lung cancer in developing anti-tumor activity by gambogic acid mediated mTOR signaling: in vitro and computational study.
studies.authors: Bo S, Liao Y, Chen X, Liu C, Pang J

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Computational (network pharmacology and docking) plus in vitro study: gambogic acid is cytotoxic and pro-apoptotic in A549 lung cancer cells and docks most strongly to AKT and the mTOR effector S6K1 (RPS6KB1). Direct mTOR kinase inhibition was not measured; no in vivo or human data.

studies.title: Testosterone propionate maintains autophagic flux and mitochondrial integrity via regulation of the LC3B/p62/Beclin-1/mTOR axis in induced liver fibrosis.
studies.authors: Verma S, Vaishnav S, Yadav M, Verma A, Washimkar K

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Testosterone propionate protects against CCl4-induced liver fibrosis by maintaining mTOR-regulated autophagic flux via the LC3B/p62/Beclin-1 axis, preserving mitochondrial integrity; castration worsens fibrosis by impairing this pathway.

studies.title: Notoginsenoside R1 Alleviates Acetaminophen-Induced Liver Injury via MAPK/mTOR-Mediated Autophagy.
studies.authors: Li S, Liu Z, Pan G, Li Y, Lv K
studies.journal: The American Journal of Chinese Medicine

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: Notoginsenoside R1 alleviates acetaminophen-induced acute liver injury by activating protective autophagy through MAPK/mTOR pathway modulation, reducing hepatocyte death and oxidative damage.

studies.title: mTOR at the nexus of nutrition, growth, ageing and disease

evidence.label: Review — secondary literature, not a new result
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.finding: The flagship modern review of the whole field, from Sabatini's own lab (Nature Reviews Molecular Cell Biology). Maps 25+ years of mTOR biology - how it senses nutrients, controls growth and autophagy, and goes wrong in cancer, neurodegeneration, metabolic disease and aging. The single best orientation document for the entire Atlas.

studies.title: FLCN loss is characterized by SQSTM1/p62 accumulation despite functional autophagy flux in Birt-Hogg-Dubé syndrome-associated kidney cancer
studies.authors: Ullern H; Johannessen JA; Kasikci F; Formica M; Karimi Melve N; Andresen S; Brech A; Axcrona K; Jørgensen K; Farkas L; Enserink JM; Knævelsrud H

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: BHD patient-derived kidney cancer cell line; Norwegian BHD patient tumor cohort
studies.finding: In BHD patient-derived kidney cancer cells, FLCN loss causes constitutive nuclear TFEB localization and mTORC1 hyperactivation, but leaves bulk autophagy flux and LC3 lipidation unaffected; however, the autophagy receptor SQSTM1/p62 accumulates in enlarged puncta, a finding replicated in a Norwegian cohort of BHD patient kidney tumors, showing p62 accumulation is dissociable from bulk autophagic flux.

studies.title: A systems study reveals concurrent activation of AMPK and mTOR by amino acids
studies.authors: Dalle Pezze P; Ruf S; Sonntag AG; Langelaar-Makkinje M; Hall P; Heberle AM; Razquin Navas P; van Eunen K; Tölle RC; Schwarz JJ; Wiese H; Warscheid B; Deitersen J; Stork B; Fäßler E; Schäuble S; Hahn U; Horvatovich P; Shanley DP; Thedieck K

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Human cell lines; amino acid re-addition time courses, quantitative proteomics and dynamic modelling
studies.finding: Adding amino acids back to starved cells switched on AMPK, PI3K and mTORC2 acutely and independently of mTORC1, at the same time as mTOR. AMPK activation ran through CaMKK-beta and, under amino acid sufficiency, AMPK kept autophagy going via ULK1. So the textbook picture of AMPK and mTORC1 as simple opposites does not hold in the first minutes after feeding - which matters for how the AMPK-ULK1 feedback arm behaves over time.

relations.mechanism: In the nucleus TFEB switches on a whole gene programme for autophagy and for building new lysosomes - the cell's recycling capacity, not just a single step.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Once inside the nucleus, TFEB switches on a whole set of genes for cleanup and for building new lysosomes.
relations.context: Same flux caveat as ULK1-AUTOPHAGY: TFEB target-gene induction (more lysosomes, more autophagy machinery transcribed) is not itself proof that degradative flux increased - it raises capacity, which still needs to be confirmed with a flux readout rather than assumed from expression alone.
relations.note: The transcriptional arm of autophagy, distinct from the fast ULK1 arm.

relations.mechanism: Freed ULK1 nucleates the autophagosome - the self-eating programme that recycles damaged parts and is the leading candidate mechanism for mTOR inhibition's benefits.
relations.mechanism_beginner: Freed ULK1 kicks off autophagy – the cell's recycling programme, and the leading idea for why blocking this pathway might be beneficial.
relations.context: LC3-II accumulation, the standard readout for this step, marks autophagosome number, not flux: it rises whether autophagosomes are being made faster or degraded slower (e.g. under lysosomal/fusion block), so it cannot alone distinguish increased autophagy from stalled autophagy. A flux assay (e.g. LC3-II with and without a degradation blocker, or p62 turnover) is needed to tell the two apart.
